question: What is the main reason we study and use nursing theories in the clinic?

options.A: To guide clinical judgement and patient care
options.B: To increase the cost of hospital administration
options.C: To replace medical diagnoses in hospital wards
options.D: To eliminate the need for nursing documentation

explanation: Nursing theories aren't just for exams! They give us a clear roadmap for how to assess, plan, and look after our patients every single day. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h1)

question: How do nursing models differ from nursing theories?

options.A: Theories focus only on equipment while models focus on patients
options.B: Models are visual representations that translate abstract theories into practical tools
options.C: Theories are used by doctors whereas models are used by nurses
options.D: Models are strict laws while theories are mere guesses

explanation: Think of a theory as a big idea, and a model as a picture or diagram that helps you actually use that idea at the bedside! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h1)

question: What is the main focus of Florence Nightingale's Environmental Theory?

options.C: Manipulating the patient's surroundings to aid recovery
options.D: Performing advanced surgical procedures in clinics

explanation: Nightingale was all about the healing power of nature! She believed that fixing up a patient's surroundings—like fresh air and cleanliness—helps them get better faster. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h2)

question: A nurse opens the ward windows and clears away stagnant water containers. Whose theory is this nurse putting into practice?
explanation: Spot on! Fresh air, clean water, and a tidy environment are the absolute heart of Florence Nightingale's famous theory. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h2)

question: How did Virginia Henderson simply describe the unique role of a nurse?

options.A: Assisting individuals to perform activities they would do unaided if able
options.B: Prescribing pharmacological therapies based on hospital protocols
options.C: Managing financial budgets for community health centers
options.D: Acting as the primary diagnostic agent for infectious diseases

explanation: Henderson saw the nurse as someone who helps patients do the things they would normally do for themselves if they had the strength, will, or knowledge. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h3)

question: A nurse feeds a weak patient who cannot hold a spoon. Which basic need from Henderson's model is being met here?
explanation: You got it! Helping a patient with their meals directly fulfills the basic need for proper nutrition and hydration. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h3)

question: When does a 'self-care deficit' happen according to Dorothea Orem?

options.A: When visiting hours are restricted by ward management
options.B: When a doctor refuses to sign the patient's treatment chart
options.C: When self-care demand is greater than the patient's agency
options.D: When the hospital runs out of essential medical supplies

explanation: In plain terms, a self-care deficit occurs when a patient needs to take care of themselves, but their current health condition makes them unable to do so. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h4)

question: A stroke patient is totally dependent on the nurses for turning, feeding, and bathing. Which of Orem's nursing systems is this?
explanation: Because the patient cannot do anything for themselves right now, the nurse has to do *all* the caring—that is a 'wholly' (completely) compensatory system! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why is it important to consider local culture when using Western nursing theories in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Local hospitals do not permit the use of written nursing care plans
options.B: Nigerian patients refuse all forms of institutional medications
options.C: Family members actively participate in daily patient care tasks
options.D: Standard nursing theories contradict traditional African governance

explanation: In our culture, family members are always around to support and help care for loved ones in the hospital, so our nursing approach must welcome them! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h5)

question: A nurse in a busy Lagos hospital uses Henderson's basic needs to prioritize care in a crowded ward. What is the main benefit of this?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing hospital equipment
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for doctors to write prescriptions
options.C: It ensures critical physiological needs are met despite staff shortages
options.D: It prevents patients from ever being discharged from the ward

explanation: When the ward is full and staff are stretched thin, focusing on basic needs like breathing, eating, and hygiene helps nurses tackle the most urgent care first! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h5)
